title: A Simpler Way: The Umbrella Example

steps.title: Real-world intuition
steps.say: Forget the curves for a second—think of umbrellas when a sudden rainstorm hits. Far more buyers suddenly compete for the same goods.

ops.text:
Everyday intuition:

Sunny day: 10 umbrellas,
10 buyers at $10.

Sudden rainstorm:
50 buyers rush to buy!

steps.title: Shortage at the old price
steps.say: At the old price P1, sellers only have Q1 umbrellas, but way more people want one now. That gap is a shortage.

ops.text:
1. Shortage at old price:
Only Q1 are on the shelf.
Many buyers leave empty-handed.

steps.title: Buyers bid up the price
steps.say: Because buyers don't want to get soaked, they offer more money. That bidding war pushes the price up.

ops.text:
2. Bidding war:
Buyers compete:
"I'll pay $15!" "I'll pay $20!"
Price climbs up.

steps.title: New equilibrium
steps.say: The price keeps rising until supply and demand balance out again at E2, with a higher price P2.

ops.text:
3. New balance at E2:
Price is higher (P2),
shortage is resolved!
